They know it, the new government of Peru knows it. But it is a step. And welcome, Betssy Chávez, to Mexico." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, on Peru Peru granted safe-conduct to Betssy Chávez, Pedro Castillo's former prime minister, asylee at Mexico's Lima embassy since December 2022. A Mexican Air Force plane flew her to Mexico today. Peru broke relations in 2022; Brazil guarded the embassy in between.

🇲🇽📉 Mexico's annual inflation falls to 3.12% in July. "Annual inflation in Mexico falls to 3.12 percent. We were at 3.37 in June and July came in at 3.12 percent. Very important." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, morning press conference July inflation eased from 3.37% in June and stays inside the central bank's target range. Sheinbaum credited the PASIC basic-basket price agreement (~913 pesos/week), voluntary gasoline and diesel price caps, and the tomato supply deal.

🇲🇽🍺 <u>MEXICO, WORLD BEER KING: $6.3 BILLION IN EXPORTS</u>

On International Beer Day, Mexico toasts as the world’s top exporter: 6,267 million dollars sold abroad in 2025, El Economista reports, with a domestic market moving nearly 485,000 million pesos. The chain runs from barley fields to malting plants, glass and aluminum factories, breweries and logistics hubs — hundreds of thousands of jobs — all the way to the corner store. ENCODAT 2025: 8 of every 10 alcohol consumers in Mexico choose beer. Fourth-largest producer on the planet, and aiming for third.

🇲🇽💧 <u>TLÁHUAC: NINE DRAINAGE WORKS TO END DECADES OF FLOODING</u>

Clara Brugada supervised nine priority hydraulic works in Tláhuac — an investment of more than 256 million pesos that will directly benefit 36,000 residents, renewing the storm drainage network and mitigating sinkholes and cracks in vulnerable neighborhoods. "The time has come to prevent more flooding in this area," the Mexico City head of government said. Borough mayor Berenice Hernández says the works bring "tranquility, well-being and security" to communities whose petitions were postponed for years.

🇲🇽🛢️ <u>FRACKING: SCIENCE PANEL RULES OUT TAMPICO-MISANTLA — WATER TEST COMES FIRST</u>

Mexico’s scientific committee on non-conventional gas recommended prohibiting fracking in the Tampico-Misantla basin and limiting any evaluation to Sabinas-Burro-Picachos and Burgos. The first step is not gas wells but hydrogeological exploration by the Mexican Institute of Water Technology. Sheinbaum: "if there is no salt water, the possibility of any non-conventional gas exploitation is closed." Today she backed the scientific route with two conditions attached: protection of water and citizen consultations before anything moves.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>AYOTZINAPA: FORMER GUERRERO GOVERNOR JAILED OVER HIDDEN VIDEOS</u>

Ángel Aguirre Rivero woke up in El Altiplano today. The FGR says the Estrella de Oro bus 1531 carrying the 43 students was videotaped by cameras 12 and 15 outside Iguala’s Palacio de Justicia as municipal and state police detained them — footage officials claimed for years "did not exist due to technical failures." That version was false. In January a collaborator revealed who extracted the recordings and delivered them directly to the then-governor. Sheinbaum this morning: the detention "is not a political matter," but the result of months of prosecutorial work, including phone-evidence analysis. Twelve years later, the "historical truth" keeps collapsing.

🇲🇽📉 <u>INFLATION FALLS TO 3.12% — LOWEST JULY IN A DECADE</u>

INEGI reported July inflation at 3.12% annually, the lowest reading for a month of July in ten years, with the consumer price index barely moving 0.03% in the month. Sheinbaum called it "good news" this morning. The figure lands a day after Banxico held its rate at 6.5% in a second straight pause, projecting even lower inflation ahead. Mexico’s prices keep cooling while the peso trades at its strongest levels of the year.

🇲🇽🌎 <u>MEXICO AND PERU RESTORE DIPLOMATIC TIES AFTER 9-MONTH RUPTURE</u>

Mexico and Peru agreed today to resume diplomatic relations, citing the "historic bonds of brotherhood, friendship and cooperation" between the two countries. Lima broke ties in November 2025 after Mexico granted asylum to former prime minister Betssy Chávez — a decision Mexico always defended as legitimate under international law. Mexico never broke the relationship; Peru did. Now Chávez has her safe-conduct and is already traveling to Mexico, foreign minister Velasco has spoken with his Peruvian counterpart Carlos Espá, and Keiko Fujimori says she will name an ambassador to Mexico in the coming days.
